record_body:
Account summary
- Enterprise prospect evaluating Redwood Dedicated in VPC for customer support + internal ops workflows.
- Primary motivator: predictable latency + data isolation, but they have real peak patterns and do not want to permanently over-provision.
- "Burst" is flagged as a gating item by both Eng and Finance.

Firmographics / environment
- Company: Northbridge Payments (NA HQ; multi-region presence)
- Current stack: Kubernetes + internal gateway; mix of OpenAI API + pilot self-hosted vLLM for a few internal apps.
- Deployment preference: VPC Dedicated only (no public hosted traffic). Wants regional pinning (us-east primary, us-west DR later).

Use cases & workloads (as described by customer)
- Support agent assistant (chat + tool calling)
  - Spike-driven: customer support volume peaks during business hours (Mon–Fri, 9am–1pm ET).
  - Tail latency sensitivity: wants predictable p95/p99 for tool-augmented responses (they measure “agent waiting time”).
- Summarization of case notes + call transcripts (batch-ish)
  - Weekly spikes: Monday mornings + end-of-month processing.
  - Acceptable degradation: can tolerate slower throughput overnight, but not during business hours.
- Internal doc search (embeddings + reranking)
  - Lower latency criticality; more cost sensitive.

Key requirements (Dedicated + Burst)
- Dedicated baseline capacity sized to “typical day.” Wants a contractable burst mechanism for short spikes (minutes to a few hours).
- Burst guardrails requested (their words were "hard rails"):
  - Max burst concurrency per tenant + optional model-level caps.
  - Max tokens/sec or equivalent throughput cap during burst.
  - Cooldown/backoff to prevent thrash when burst pools are saturated.
  - Explicit time window controls (they asked: "Can we forbid burst at month-end close?"—answer: TBD; they want it).
- Noisy neighbor protection:
  - They are fine sharing a burst pool if it has strict admission control and they can see when/why they’re denied.
  - Security team asked whether shared burst pools are physically separate from hosted fleet and how isolation is enforced.
- Fail/deny semantics:
  - If burst denied, they want deterministic behavior (either 429 with retry-after + reason, or a clear 503 with guidance).
  - They do NOT want “silent fallbacks” to unknown regions/models without explicit configuration.

Pricing / commercial notes
- Pricing sensitivity: Finance wants predictable maximum monthly exposure.
  - Asked for an included burst headroom amount as part of Dedicated + fixed overage rate, OR the ability to buy pre-paid burst credits.
  - Quote from procurement call recap: "We can’t sign if burst is open-ended; need a cap or a commit." 
- They are okay with shadow metering during pilot as long as it produces a reconciliation report they can validate.
- They asked whether burst usage could be separated on invoice lines from baseline Dedicated usage (treat as add-on SKU).

Security/compliance notes
- Requirements explicitly stated:
  - SSO/SAML for console access
  - Audit logs for config changes (who changed burst limits/enablement)
  - KMS integration expectations (they’re on AWS; asked about customer-managed keys in VPC)
  - Retention controls for logs/telemetry; they asked for a default retention statement for burst-related logs
  - Data residency: US-only for this phase
- Open questions from their security team:
  - How are burst pools isolated from other tenants and from hosted? (they asked for a written topology statement)
  - What attributes are written to logs during burst (tenant id, pool id, region, deny reason)? Need to ensure no sensitive prompt content is logged.

Activity timeline (recent)
- 2025-06-18: Technical deep dive (Fireflies: ff-2025-06-18-technical-deep-dive-burst-capacity). Topics: baseline vs burst routing, deny semantics, metrics they can monitor.
- 2025-06-24: Pricing working session: requested "burst included headroom" concept + overage rate and a monthly cap option.
- 2025-07-02: Follow-up with Eng lead: they shared peak-hour graphs (not attached here) and asked for recommended starting limits (max concurrent + TPS).
- 2025-07-10: Security Q&A #1: focus on shared burst pools + audit logging; they asked for documentation and a short written FAQ they can forward internally.

Deal team / contacts (internal)
- Owner: Markus Klein
- SE: Ravi Menon (routing/fallback questions)
- Pricing support: Laura Bennett looped for packaging/pricing questions

What we think will close this deal
- Provide a clear burst SKU definition + contract language: what is guaranteed vs best-effort.
- Provide customer-visible metrics: burst admitted/denied counts, time-in-burst, and a simple deny-reason breakdown.
- Provide a written statement on isolation boundaries + audit log coverage for burst config changes.

Risks
- If we can’t offer predictable pricing guardrails (cap/commit) for burst, they may default to AWS Bedrock or keep self-hosting a "buffer" cluster.
- They are wary of any solution that looks like preemptible capacity; they prefer strict admission control and clear denies over eviction.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Confirm which deny status codes we will standardize on for burst-denied and what Retry-After guidance looks like.
- Confirm whether we can support time-window based burst policies (even if v1 is limited).
- Provide draft of Dedicated + Burst add-on pricing model and a sample monthly bill breakdown (baseline vs burst lines).
